page_title: Plainsay — Free, open-source dictation for Mac

summary.name: Plainsay
summary.one_liner: Plainsay is a free, open-source Mac dictation app that turns speech into text at the cursor in any text field, with on-device Local mode and an optional paid Cloud service.
use_cases: quick replies and messages by voice
talking through ideas in a notes app
adding names and product terms to a dictation vocabulary
summary.what_it_does: Plainsay is a native Mac app that records speech when you press a dictation key (hold to talk or tap to start and stop) and places the resulting text at the cursor in the app you are using. Local mode runs speech recognition on your Mac using Whisper or Parakeet models, which require a one-time model download, and keeps recorded audio on the device. An optional Polishing step tidies filler words and punctuation; it can be sent to a hosted provider or a compatible local provider. Free features include history, vocabulary, and voice filtering. If text cannot be inserted into a field, the app keeps it on the clipboard.
notable: MIT-licensed Mac client with source available on GitHub
Free Local mode with no account, subscription, or usage quotas
Optional paid Cloud tier (US$4/month) for hosted transcription and Polishing
No analytics in the Mac client
caveats: Requires macOS 14 or later and Apple silicon
Cloud tier is paid, not open source, and capped at 900 transcription minutes per rolling 30 days
Selected-text AI rewrites need the user's own provider key; a Cloud subscription alone does not enable them
Some text fields do not support reliable insertion, so users may need to paste manually
